title: Sophos Endpoint tamper protection passwords
use_case: After a Sophos Fusion admin account is compromised, give every device in the groups you list a new tamper protection password, turn tamper protection back on where it's off, and record what changed on the case.
trigger: User Initiated: a Response Action on Case, which an analyst runs from the case about the compromise. Leave When does this playbook run? at Always.
connections: Unofficial_SophosEndpoint 1.0.0, the Sophos Endpoint connector from this library: OAuth client credentials with a Sophos Fusion API credential
Taegis.Case 1.0.5, the case connector Sophos manages, to comment on the case
requires: Sophos Endpoint devices with tamper protection, a Sophos Fusion API credential for the connector, and Sophos Fusion playbooks under Security Operations > Automations
mdr_note: Sophos MDR doesn't run or watch this playbook. A new password stops anyone who knew the old one, Sophos MDR included, from using it; MDR reads the new one in Sophos Fusion as you do.
rollback: Nothing brings back an old password. Read each new password in Sophos Fusion on the device page. Tamper protection the playbook turned on can be turned off there.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: This playbook gives every device in the groups you list a new tamper protection password and turns tamper protection back on where it's off, then reads them back and comments on the case. An analyst runs it from the case about a compromised Sophos Fusion admin, and it calls the library's Sophos Endpoint connector. Dry run is on, and only the device groups you list are in scope.
notes:
Setup:
- Run it from the case about the compromise, after you have locked the compromised admin out. An admin who can still sign in can read the new passwords too.
- List every group whose devices the admin could reach. Most devices per run has to cover them all, up to 1000.

How it works:
- An admin who can sign in to Sophos Fusion can read every device's tamper protection password and turn tamper protection off.
- It lists the devices in the groups, sends the new-password requests in batches of 200, and turns tamper protection on in a separate request, so a device that can't go on still gets its new password.
- It reads up to 50 devices back and lists any whose password didn't change. No password appears in the comment or the execution.

Testing:
- On 2026-11-08 the dsl passed playbookValidateDSLV2 with no errors or warnings in a Sophos Fusion test tenant in eu02. A renamed copy imported with its connector, exported again unchanged apart from the tenant's own fields, and was deleted.
- It ran by hand on a test case, in dry run and live, against a group holding one offline Windows test device. Live, the device got a new password, confirmed by the playbook's read-back and separately through the API, and the turn-on was accepted. The execution log held no password.

Known gaps:
- Tamper protection was off for the test tenant, so turning it on was accepted but changed nothing. A tenant with it on is untested.
- More than one page of devices, and batches past the first 200, are untested.
